fence_surface_input_groups.description: Fence has a single primary paintable item (ITM_FENCE_FIELD, SF). PaintScope delivers final SF after (LF x Height x 2) and fence_style geometric multiplier. Gate hardware count is EA-based for masking tasks. All protection inputs are LF or SF based.

task_production_rates.name: Landscape Protection Along Fence Base (Both Sides)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Deploy drop cloths and plastic sheeting along fence base on both sides to protect landscaping, mulch beds, and ground cover from stain drip and overspray. ~29 sec per LF. Includes staking/weighting at grade. LF of fence line — applied to both sides during two-pass application.

defect_tolerance.all: Full coverage along fence base both sides. Tarps secured against wind. No gaps where stain could drip onto plantings or mulch.

task_production_rates.name: Hardscape Protection Along Fence Line
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Lay drop cloths on walkways, driveways, and patios running along fence line. ~14 sec per SF. Stain on concrete is extremely difficult to remove — critical protection zone. Same rate as deck hardscape protection.

defect_tolerance.all: Full coverage of adjacent hardscape within overspray zone. Drop cloths secured at edges. No gaps at fence-to-hardscape transition.

task_production_rates.name: Siding Protection at Fence-to-House Junction
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Mask siding at fence-to-house junction with plastic sheeting taped at top edge, 4-6 ft height coverage. ~36 sec per LF. Includes taping top edge, securing bottom, and ensuring no gaps at fence attachment point. LF of house wall at fence tie.

defect_tolerance.all: Full coverage of siding face at fence tie. Plastic secured at top and bottom. No gaps at fence attachment point.

task_production_rates.name: Neighbor Property Line Protection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Deploy protection along neighbor's property line when spraying fence side facing neighbor. Drop cloth along neighbor's fence base, communicate with neighbor about overspray risk. ~45 min average. Includes coordination time. Highly variable by fence length and neighbor's landscaping complexity.

defect_tolerance.all: Neighbor's landscaping and structures protected. Drop cloth secured along fence base on neighbor's side. Neighbor notified.

task_production_rates.name: Gate Hardware Masking/Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Mask or remove gate hardware (hinges, latches, locks, handles) per gate. ~12 min per gate. Includes taping around hardware that cannot be removed and removing hardware that can be. Gate hardware is exposed to stain from both sides.

defect_tolerance.all: All hardware masked or removed. Tape edges secure. No exposed metal surfaces that could be stained.

task_production_rates.name: Fence Moisture Content Testing
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Pin-type moisture meter readings at multiple points along fence line. MC >19% for PT pine or >15% for cedar is HARD STOP. ~20 min for standard fence (multiple test points per section, both sides). Mandatory for ALL wood conditions. Includes documentation of readings.

defect_tolerance.all: Multiple test points along fence documented. All readings below threshold. Wet sections flagged for re-test.

task_production_rates.name: Seasoning Period Verification
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Verify pressure-treated wood seasoning period from install date. PT pine requires 3-6 months seasoning before coating (ACQ treatment). Water bead test on surface — beading indicates preservative still active. Administrative verification + water sprinkle test. ~12 min. HARD STOP if seasoning period insufficient.

defect_tolerance.all: Install date verified. Water absorption test performed. Seasoning period confirmed adequate. No beading on test areas.

task_production_rates.name: Mill Glaze Removal Sanding
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Sand new milled fence boards with 80-grit to remove mill glaze and open grain for stain penetration. ~55 sec per SF. Random orbital or belt sander on flat panels, hand sand on posts and rails. Vertical surfaces are slightly faster than horizontal deck because gravity assists dust removal. Mandatory for new milled wood.

defect_tolerance.all: All mill glaze removed. Water droplet test shows immediate absorption. Uniform open grain across all panels and posts.

task_production_rates.name: Fence Pressure Wash
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Pressure wash fence surface at 1,000-1,500 PSI (wood-safe pressure). ~9 sec per SF. Fan tip, maintain 12-18 inch distance. Removes dirt, mildew, gray weathered fiber, and chemical residue. Vertical fence surfaces shed water faster than horizontal decks — same application rate, faster dry. 24-48 hr dry time after (not included in rate).

defect_tolerance.all: Uniform clean surface. No gray weathered fiber remaining. No pressure damage or furring. Even pressure pattern — no striping.

task_production_rates.name: Mildew Treatment
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply mildew treatment solution (sodium hypochlorite or oxygen bleach), allow dwell, scrub, rinse. ~24 sec per SF. Required when visible mildew or algae present. Fence shaded sides are prone to mildew in humid climates. Treatment must kill spores before staining.

defect_tolerance.all: All visible mildew eliminated. Surface passes bleach test. No residue remaining.

task_production_rates.name: Fence Refinishing Sand
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Refinishing sand with 80-100 grit for previously coated or weathered fence surfaces. ~72 sec per SF. Removes loose/flaking coating, smooths raised grain. Belt sander or random orbital on panels, hand sand on posts. Slower than mill glaze sand due to old coating removal effort.

defect_tolerance.all: All loose coating removed. Raised grain smoothed. Uniform surface profile. No deep gouges from sanding.

task_production_rates.name: Chemical Stripper Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply alkaline fence stripper by pump sprayer. ~13 sec per SF. Even coverage required for uniform stripping. Work in manageable sections. Vertical surfaces — product runs down so work top-to-bottom in sections. Part of 3-step chemical restoration for weathered wood.

defect_tolerance.all: Even application across entire surface. No dry spots. Maintained wet edge. Working top-to-bottom on vertical surface.

task_production_rates.name: Stripper Dwell Time
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Allow chemical stripper to dwell on surface per manufacturer specification. ~15-20 min. Crew monitors for drying and re-wets if needed. Vertical surfaces dry faster than horizontal decks — may need more re-wetting. Fixed time per application cycle.

defect_tolerance.all: Dwell time per manufacturer spec. Surface kept wet throughout dwell period. No premature drying on vertical faces.

task_production_rates.name: Stripper Agitation/Scrub
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Scrub stripper into fence surface with stiff bristle brush. ~24 sec per SF. Agitates chemical into wood grain and loosens old coating. Labor-intensive on vertical surfaces — gravity helps rinse but scrubbing is against gravity. Work same sections as application.

defect_tolerance.all: All sections scrubbed uniformly. Old coating visibly loosening. No skipped areas.

task_production_rates.name: Stripper Rinse
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Pressure rinse stripped surface at 1,000-1,500 PSI to remove chemical residue and loosened coating. ~9 sec per SF. Fan tip, maintain distance. Vertical surfaces drain well — same rate as deck rinse. Thorough rinse critical — residual stripper prevents stain adhesion.

defect_tolerance.all: All chemical residue removed. No stripper film remaining. Clean wood surface visible. Water runs clear.

task_production_rates.name: Wood Brightener Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply acid-based wood brightener (oxalic acid for cedar, citric acid alternative) by pump sprayer. ~13 sec per SF. Neutralizes alkaline stripper, restores natural wood color, opens grain. Same application rate as stripper. For cedar: also neutralizes tannin staining.

defect_tolerance.all: Even application across entire surface. No dry spots. Wood color visibly brightening within minutes.

task_production_rates.name: Brightener Dwell Time
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Allow wood brightener to dwell per manufacturer spec. ~10-15 min. Shorter dwell than stripper. Crew monitors for even color change. Fixed time per application cycle.

defect_tolerance.all: Dwell time per manufacturer spec. Uniform color change visible. No premature rinse.

task_production_rates.name: Brightener Rinse
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Pressure rinse brightened surface at 1,000-1,500 PSI. ~9 sec per SF. Remove all chemical residue. Same rate as stripper rinse. 12-24 hr dry time required before staining (shorter than deck due to vertical drainage — not included in rate).

defect_tolerance.all: All brightener residue removed. Wood shows natural color. No chemical film remaining. Surface pH neutral.

task_production_rates.name: Post-Wash Dry Verification
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Verify fence surface has dried to acceptable MC after washing or chemical restoration. Pin-type moisture meter at multiple points. Confirm MC below threshold (19% PT pine, 15% cedar). ~12 min. May require return visit if not dry (12-24 hr dry time after chemical restoration — shorter than deck due to vertical drainage).

defect_tolerance.all: All test points below MC threshold. No visible wet spots. Surface ready for stain/paint application.

task_production_rates.name: Tannin-Blocking / Exterior Primer Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray or roll primer on fence surface. ~14 sec per SF. Tannin-blocking primer (shellac-based) for cedar substrate with solid stain or paint. Standard exterior acrylic primer for PT pine with paint. Conditional task — only for solid_stain on cedar or paint on any substrate. Penetrating stains (transparent, semi-transparent) do NOT use primer.

defect_tolerance.all: Full coverage with no holidays. Even film build. No runs or sags on vertical surfaces. Tannin bleed blocked on cedar.

applies_when.notes: Cedar requires tannin-blocking primer for solid stain and paint. PT pine requires standard primer for paint only. Penetrating stains skip primer entirely.

task_production_rates.name: Fence Stain — Spray + Back-Brush (Coat 1)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray stain onto fence panels followed immediately by back-brushing to work stain into wood grain. 215 SF/hr per 2-person crew-hour (sprayer + brusher). Doctrine rate for fence spray_backbrush. Back-brushing is MANDATORY for penetrating stains — spray alone does not force stain into grain. Spray/backbrush coupling: spray rate (215) <= backbrush rate (215) — compliant. Vertical surface — work top-to-bottom, one side at a time.

defect_tolerance.all: Even penetration across all boards. No runs or sags on vertical surface. Back-brushed within 30 seconds of spray. Consistent color. No dry edges.

task_production_rates.name: Fence Stain — Brush Application (Coat 1)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush-only stain application on fence. 120 SF/hr doctrine rate. ~30 sec per SF. 4-inch stain brush, work with grain, maintain wet edge board-by-board. Excellent penetration but slow. Primary method for split rail fences, detail work, and small fences. Single worker.

defect_tolerance.all: Even penetration. No brush marks visible after absorption. Consistent color board to board. Wet edge maintained.

task_production_rates.name: Fence Stain — Roller Application (Coat 1)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Roller application of stain on fence using 3/4 inch nap roller. ~27 sec per SF. Faster than brush, good for flat privacy fence panels. Less grain penetration than brush — best for solid stains where film-build matters. Back-brush roller laps if penetrating stain. Single worker.

defect_tolerance.all: Even coverage. No roller marks after drying. Consistent film build. No runs on vertical surface.

task_production_rates.name: Fence Paint — Spray Application (Coat 1)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray paint (exterior acrylic latex) onto fence surface. ~12 sec per SF. Paint sprays faster than stain — higher viscosity means better film build per pass with less back-brushing (film-forming, not penetrating). No mandatory back-brush for paint. Vertical surface — work top-to-bottom. LEAST RECOMMENDED coating type.

defect_tolerance.all: Even film build. No runs or sags on vertical surface. Consistent coverage. No holidays. No overspray on adjacent surfaces.

task_production_rates.name: Fence Paint — Brush Application (Coat 1)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush-only paint application on fence. ~29 sec per SF. Exterior acrylic latex with 3-4 inch brush. Work with grain on boards, cross-stroke on posts. Better film build control than roller on rough-sawn boards. Single worker.

defect_tolerance.all: Even film build. No brush marks after leveling. Consistent coverage. No runs on vertical surfaces.

task_production_rates.name: Fence Paint — Roller Application (Coat 1)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Roller application of exterior paint on fence using 3/4 inch nap roller. ~24 sec per SF. Faster than brush on flat privacy panels. Good film build on smooth surfaces. Rough-sawn boards need heavier nap. Single worker.

defect_tolerance.all: Even film build. No roller marks after leveling. Consistent coverage. No runs on vertical surface.

task_production_rates.name: Fence Stain — Spray + Back-Brush (Coat 2)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Second coat spray + back-brush. Same rate as coat 1 (215 SF/hr). First coat seals grain — second coat sits on more consistent surface but still requires back-brushing for solid stain. Conditional on coating_type = solid_stain (penetrating stains are typically single-coat on fences).

defect_tolerance.all: Even coverage over first coat. No pooling or runs. Consistent color depth. Maintain wet edge.

task_production_rates.name: Fence Stain — Brush Application (Coat 2)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Second coat brush application. Same rate as coat 1 (120 SF/hr). Conditional on coating_type = solid_stain.

defect_tolerance.all: Even coverage over first coat. Consistent color depth. No brush marks after leveling.

task_production_rates.name: Fence Stain — Roller Application (Coat 2)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Second coat roller application. Same rate as coat 1 (135 SF/hr). Conditional on coating_type = solid_stain.

defect_tolerance.all: Even coverage over first coat. Consistent film build. No roller marks.

task_production_rates.name: Fence Paint — Spray Application (Coat 2)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Second coat spray paint. Same rate as coat 1 (300 SF/hr). Standard exterior paint 2-coat protocol. Full dry between coats (4-24 hours).

defect_tolerance.all: Even film build over first coat. No runs or sags. Consistent coverage and sheen.

task_production_rates.name: Fence Paint — Brush Application (Coat 2)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Second coat brush paint. Same rate as coat 1 (125 SF/hr).

defect_tolerance.all: Even film build over first coat. Consistent coverage. No brush marks after leveling.

task_production_rates.name: Fence Paint — Roller Application (Coat 2)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Second coat roller paint. Same rate as coat 1 (150 SF/hr).

defect_tolerance.all: Even film build over first coat. Consistent coverage. No roller marks.

task_production_rates.name: Final Walkthrough Inspection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Walk entire fence line inspecting both sides for holidays, uneven color, missed spots at board joints and post tops, runs/sags on vertical surfaces. ~22 min for standard residential fence. Includes paint option risk warning documentation if coating_type = paint.

defect_tolerance.all: Complete visual inspection of all stained/painted surfaces both sides. No missed spots. Color consistency verified. No runs on vertical surfaces. Paint risk documented if applicable.

task_production_rates.name: Touch-Up Staining/Painting
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush touch-up of defects found during final inspection. ~48 sec per SF. Rate is per total field SF — most area passes without touch-up. Includes spot re-staining holidays, evening out color variations, and fixing runs/sags found on inspection walk.

defect_tolerance.all: All defects repaired. Touch-ups blended into surrounding stain/paint. No visible repair boundaries after drying.

task_production_rates.name: Gate Hardware Reinstallation
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Reinstall removed gate hardware and remove masking from non-removed hardware. ~12 min per gate. Includes verifying gate operation after reinstall and checking for stain/paint on hardware.

defect_tolerance.all: All hardware reinstalled and functional. Gate operates correctly. No stain/paint residue on hardware. No tape residue.

task_production_rates.name: Protection Material Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove all protection materials — landscape drops (both sides), hardscape covers, siding masking, neighbor property line drops. ~20 min. Check for tape residue on siding. Verify no stain on protected surfaces.

defect_tolerance.all: All protection materials removed. No tape residue on siding. No stain on protected surfaces. Both sides of fence cleared.

task_production_rates.name: Tool and Equipment Cleanup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Clean all staining/painting equipment — flush sprayer if used, clean brushes, rollers, trays. Dispose of used abrasives and chemical containers. ~17 min. Stain cleanup is faster than paint cleanup (thinner product, easier flush).

defect_tolerance.all: All tools cleaned and stored. Sprayer flushed. Chemical containers properly disposed. Site debris removed.

factor_modifiers.name: Coating Type Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Coating type is the PRIMARY configuration dimension for fence specs (replaces quality_tier). Affects application rate — transparent is fastest (lowest viscosity, no color matching), paint is slowest (full prime-paint pipeline, edge management). Material consumption handled separately by coverage profiles.
factor_modifiers.notes: Semi_transparent is baseline (1.00). Transparent is 15% faster (thin product, minimal working). Solid stain is 15% slower (film-forming, more careful application for uniform appearance). Paint is 30% slower (full prime-paint pipeline, edge management, risk documentation). Affects APPLICATION tasks only — prep rates are not coating-type-dependent.

factor_modifiers.name: Wood Condition Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Wood condition drives prep intensity. New wood is baseline. Weathered adds chemical restoration protocol. Previously_coated has highest prep overhead. Affects PREP tasks only — application rates are not affected because prep normalizes the surface.
factor_modifiers.notes: New milled is baseline (clean surface, mill glaze removal only). New PT seasoned is 5% slower (open grain but PT chemical residue). Weathered is 40% slower (chemical restoration, gray fiber removal). Previously_coated is 60% slower (stripping, sanding through old coating, adhesion testing). Applies to PREP tasks only — application tasks use coating_type modifier instead. Lower modifiers than deck (1.40/1.60 vs 1.50/1.75) because vertical fence surfaces have less UV/moisture damage accumulation than horizontal deck surfaces.

factor_modifiers.name: Wood Substrate Type Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Fence wood species affects prep and application rates. PT pine is baseline (~65% of residential fences). Cedar requires tannin management and is softer wood (easier to damage during prep).
factor_modifiers.notes: PT pine is baseline (dense, standard residential fence lumber). Cedar is 10% slower (softer wood requires lighter sanding pressure, tannin bleed-through adds brightener step, higher stain absorption on end grain). No redwood for fences (per resolution — cedar and PT pine only). Applies to both prep and application tasks — cedar absorbs more stain requiring slower application for even color.

quality_effects.description: Fence specs use coating_type as primary dimension instead of quality_tier. Coat count is driven by coating type, not tier.

transparent.notes: Single coat of transparent sealer. No interstage. Recoat in 1-2 years.

semi_transparent.notes: Single coat of semi-transparent stain on fences. Penetrating stain on vertical surfaces — re-stain when color fades (2-4 year cycle). Vertical surfaces don't wear like horizontal decks, so single coat is standard.

solid_stain.notes: Two coats of solid stain. Film-forming — inspect between coats for holidays, runs, sags. Full dry between coats (4-24 hours). Both sides must get coat 1 before either side gets coat 2.

paint.notes: Two coats of exterior acrylic latex paint. Standard exterior paint 2-coat protocol. Full dry between coats. Mandatory risk warning — paint on wood fences has highest delamination risk due to moisture entrapment.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: PT pine, semi-transparent, new milled — best case (spray_backbrush)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Best case — baseline fence stain production. 215 SF/hr per 2-person crew. Wood_condition modifier applies to prep tasks, not application.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: PT pine, transparent, new milled — fastest (spray_backbrush)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Transparent sealer on new PT pine — fastest possible fence production. 253 SF/hr per 2-person crew.
Cedar refinish with brush — common residential job. Substrate modifier only on application (wood_condition modifier applies to prep tasks separately). 109 SF/hr single worker.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Cedar, paint, previously coated — worst case application (spray)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Paint on cedar — slowest application combination. 210 SF/hr. Wood_condition modifier applies to prep tasks separately.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Cedar, previously coated — worst case PREP (refinish sand)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Worst case prep — previously coated cedar fence. 28 SF/hr. Slow but realistic for stripping old coating from softwood.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Maximum stacking check — paint x previously_coated x cedar (all 3 on same task if applied)
modifier_stacking_examples.tasks_affected: TSK_FNCE_PAINT_SPRAY (hypothetical — wood_condition normally applies to prep only)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Absolute worst case with all 3 modifiers stacking: 1.30 x 1.60 x 1.10 = 2.29x — well under 4.0x stacking cap. In practice, wood_condition primarily affects prep, so application stacking is typically coating_type x substrate_material only (max 1.43x).

assumptions: Base rates for spray_backbrush are per crew-hour with 2 workers (sprayer + brusher). crew_size = 2.
Base rates for brush, roll, and paint spray are per single worker. crew_size = 1.
Spray/backbrush coupling rule satisfied: spray rate <= backbrush rate (same combined rate for stain). Back-brushing is MANDATORY for penetrating stains — spray alone prohibited.
Paint spray does NOT require mandatory back-brushing (film-forming, not penetrating). crew_size = 1 for paint spray.
Coating type replaces quality tier as primary configuration dimension. No QT-based rate scaling.
FAC_FNCE_COATING_TYPE applies to APPLICATION tasks only. Prep rates are not coating-type-dependent.
FAC_FNCE_WOOD_CONDITION applies to PREP tasks only. Application rates are not affected because prep normalizes the surface.
FAC_FNCE_SUBSTRATE_TYPE applies to both prep and application tasks (cedar stain absorption affects both).
Modifier stacking is multiplicative: effective_rate = base_rate / (coating_type x wood_condition x substrate_material).
Maximum combined modifier: 2.29x (paint 1.30 x previously_coated 1.60 x cedar 1.10). Well under 4.0x stacking cap.
No FAC_EXT_ACCESS for fences — ground-level work. No height modifier needed.
fence_style geometric multiplier handled by PaintScope BEFORE SF reaches spec — NOT modeled as a production modifier.
Chemical restoration tasks (strip/brighten) are CONDITIONAL on wood_condition = weathered.
Seasoning verification is CONDITIONAL on new PT pine only.
Mill glaze sanding is CONDITIONAL on wood_condition = new.
Primer is CONDITIONAL: tannin-blocking for cedar + solid_stain/paint; standard exterior for PT pine + paint only. Penetrating stains skip primer entirely.
Coat 2 tasks are CONDITIONAL on coating_type = solid_stain or paint (film-forming coatings). Transparent and semi-transparent are single-coat on fences.
Coat 2 tasks use same rate as coat 1 — consistent technique required on both coats.
FIXED time tasks are not area-dependent. Fence length does not affect moisture testing, dwell times, or inspection fixed times.

Environmental modifiers (wind, sun, surface temp) are NOT declared as separate FAC_ entries — fence staining is ground-level work. Hot sun managed by SOP scheduling (early morning/late afternoon), not modifier. Wind blocks spray method entirely (switch to brush/roll).
Protection tasks use simple defect_tolerance (no QT split) because fence spec is not QT-driven.
PaintScope SF includes both sides of fence — per-face rates are NOT needed. Application tasks work one side at a time but total SF already accounts for both sides.
risks: Paint on wood fences has the highest delamination risk of any fence coating — moisture migrates through wood from both sides and lifts film-forming coatings. Mandatory risk warning documentation required for paint coating_type.
Previously coated fences with unknown coating type require adhesion testing before committing to coating strategy — incompatible coatings will delaminate. May require full strip regardless.

Chemical restoration (strip + brighten) adds significant time and a separate mobilization day (12-24 hr dry time). Estimator must account for return visit. Shorter dry than deck due to vertical drainage.
Cedar tannin bleed can occur through semi-transparent and transparent coatings — not a defect but requires customer expectation setting. Tannin-blocking primer only used for solid stain and paint.

Shadowbox fences (1.6x geometric multiplier from PaintScope) present spray access challenges — boards on alternating sides require multiple angle passes. May reduce effective spray_backbrush rate below 215 SF/hr baseline.
Split rail fences are brush-only — spray and roll methods are not practical on rail-only construction with large gaps. Brush rate of 120 SF/hr applies.
Neighbor property protection is highly variable — some fences have zero neighbor-side concerns, others require extensive coordination. FIXED time of 45 min is an average.
Wood condition modifier for previously_coated (1.60x) assumes standard stripping difficulty. Multi-layer old paint or epoxy-fortified coatings may exceed this modifier — flag for estimator review.
Fence spray_backbrush rate (215 SF/hr) is lower than deck (275 SF/hr) due to vertical surface — gravity causes runs, requiring more careful spray technique and faster back-brushing follow-up.
validation_plan: Time 3 spray_backbrush fence staining jobs on new PT pine to calibrate 215 SF/hr baseline per 2-person crew.
Time 2 brush-only fence staining jobs to calibrate 120 SF/hr baseline.
Time 2 roll application jobs on privacy fence flat panels to calibrate 135 SF/hr baseline.
Track chemical restoration sequences (strip + brighten + rinse) on 2 weathered fence jobs to validate combined prep time.
Compare PT pine vs cedar staining rates on similar fence geometry to validate FAC_FNCE_SUBSTRATE_TYPE 1.10x modifier.
Compare transparent vs solid stain application times on same fence to validate FAC_FNCE_COATING_TYPE modifier spread (0.85x to 1.15x).
Time paint spray application on 2 fence jobs to validate 300 SF/hr baseline and compare to stain spray_backbrush rate.
Track gate hardware masking/reinstall times across 5 gates to validate 5 EA/hr rate.
Track protection setup and teardown times across 5 fence jobs to validate FIXED time ranges.
Compare primer application rates (spray vs roll) on 2 cedar solid-stain fence jobs to validate 250 SF/hr baseline.
